name: Siwa Oasis
tagline: Egypt's most remote and distinct oasis, a Berber-speaking desert town of mudbrick ruins, salt lakes and olive groves where Alexander the Great once consulted an oracle.
highlight: Floating effortlessly in a warm salt lake at sunset, the crumbling towers of Shali's mudbrick old town glowing gold on the horizon.
shortDescription: Egypt's most remote and culturally distinct oasis, home to the Oracle Temple of Amun, the ruined mudbrick town of Shali, salt lakes and the Great Sand Sea.
metaDescription: A Siwa Oasis travel guide: the Oracle Temple, Shali Fortress, Cleopatra's Spring, salt lakes, the Great Sand Sea, food and how to plan a visit.

knownFor: The Oracle Temple, Cleopatra's Spring, the mudbrick Shali Fortress

intro: Siwa Oasis is genuinely Egypt's most remote and culturally distinct destination, a Berber-speaking desert town closer to the Libyan border than to the Nile Valley.
Its history runs genuinely deep — Alexander the Great made a famous, gruelling journey here to consult the Oracle of Amun, whose temple ruins still stand above the palm groves.
Modern Siwa genuinely revolves around mudbrick architecture, natural springs and salt lakes, and the vast dunes of the Great Sand Sea rolling away toward Libya.

whyVisit.intro: Siwa's case rests genuinely on being unlike anywhere else in Egypt, both culturally and geographically.

points.title: Siwa is genuinely culturally distinct from the rest of Egypt
points.text: A Berber Amazigh community with its own language, dress and traditions.

points.title: The history here is genuinely extraordinary
points.text: Alexander the Great's famous pilgrimage to consult the Oracle of Amun.

points.title: The mudbrick architecture is genuinely unlike anywhere else in Egypt
points.text: Shali's crumbling old town rises straight out of the oasis floor.

points.title: The natural springs and salt lakes are genuinely a real highlight
points.text: Warm, buoyant water framed by palm groves and desert.

points.title: The Great Sand Sea is genuinely right on the doorstep
points.text: Dune safaris and sandboarding roll away toward the Libyan border.

attractionsIntro: Siwa's essential sights are genuinely spread across its ancient ruins, natural springs and surrounding desert.

attractions.name: Shali Fortress

image.alt: The ruined mudbrick town of Shali Fortress in Siwa

attractions.text: Genuinely Siwa's dramatic old town, a mudbrick fortress-village largely abandoned after rare heavy rains damaged it in 1926.
attractions.tip: Genuinely climb up at sunset, when the eroded walls glow gold against the sky.

attractions.name: Temple of the Oracle of Amun

image.file: File:Siwa Oasis, Temple of the Oracle of Amun, Egypt.jpg
image.alt: The Temple of the Oracle of Amun in Siwa

attractions.text: Genuinely the site that drew Alexander the Great across the desert, an oracle so respected he had himself declared a son of the god here.
attractions.tip: Genuinely pair the visit with the nearby Temple of Amun's ruins and the view over the palm groves.

attractions.name: Cleopatra's Spring (Spring of Juba)

image.alt: Cleopatra's Spring, also known as the Spring of Juba, in Siwa

attractions.text: Genuinely a natural spring-fed pool said to have been visited by Cleopatra herself, still a popular swimming spot today.
attractions.tip: Genuinely modest swimwear is appropriate — this remains a conservative, traditional community.

attractions.name: Siwa's salt lakes

image.alt: Turquoise salt lakes around Siwa Oasis

attractions.text: Genuinely a striking landscape of turquoise pools and white salt crusts scattered around the oasis.
attractions.tip: Genuinely float in one of the lakes — the salt concentration makes sinking almost impossible.

attractions.name: The Great Sand Sea

image.alt: The dunes of the Great Sand Sea near Siwa

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the world's largest sand seas, its dunes rolling away toward the Libyan border just beyond Siwa.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a 4x4 dune safari is the classic way to experience its scale.

attractions.name: Gebel al-Mawta (Mountain of the Dead)

image.alt: Gebel al-Mawta, the Mountain of the Dead, in Siwa

attractions.text: Genuinely a small hill honeycombed with painted rock tombs from Siwa's Greco-Roman period.
attractions.tip: Genuinely ask the site guard to unlock the best-preserved tombs, which aren't always open by default.

attractions.name: Siwa's olive and date groves

image.file: File:Siwa Oasis, Houses in the desert, Egypt.jpg
image.alt: Palm groves and desert houses around Siwa Oasis

attractions.text: Genuinely the oasis's economic backbone, dense palm and olive groves fed by hundreds of natural springs.
attractions.tip: Genuinely rent a bicycle to explore the groves' quiet dirt lanes.

thingsToDoIntro: Siwa genuinely rewards a slow, unhurried pace, built around its ruins, springs and surrounding desert.

thingsToDo.title: Climb Shali Fortress at sunset

image.alt: Shali Fortress at sunset in Siwa

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential Siwa ritual, watching the light turn the old town's mudbrick walls gold.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely wear sturdy shoes — the old town's paths are uneven and partly ruined.

thingsToDo.title: Swim in Cleopatra's Spring

image.alt: Swimming in Cleopatra's Spring in Siwa

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely refreshing, easy stop, a natural pool shaded by palms right in the oasis.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely quieter early morning or late afternoon, outside the midday tour-group rush.

thingsToDo.title: Float in a salt lake

image.alt: Floating in one of Siwa's salt lakes

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely novel experience, the water's salinity keeping you effortlessly buoyant.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely avoid getting salt water in your eyes, and rinse off with fresh water afterward.

thingsToDo.title: Take a 4x4 safari into the Great Sand Sea

image.alt: A 4x4 safari into the Great Sand Sea near Siwa

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely thrilling half or full day, dune bashing across some of the Sahara's largest sand formations.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book through an experienced local operator familiar with the dunes' terrain.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the rock tombs at Gebel al-Mawta

image.alt: Rock-cut tombs at Gebel al-Mawta in Siwa

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile stop, painted tombs cut into the hillside from Siwa's Greco-Roman period.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a quick visit, easily combined with Shali Fortress in the same afternoon.

thingsToDo.title: Cycle through the palm and olive groves

image.alt: Palm groves on the outskirts of Siwa Oasis

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely peaceful way to spend an afternoon, pedalling quiet dirt lanes between springs and groves.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely rent a bicycle from almost any guesthouse in town.

foods.name: Siwan bread and tagen

bestTime.headline: October to April for comfortable desert temperatures
bestTime.summary: Siwa is genuinely best visited outside the peak summer heat, when desert days turn extremely hot.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Siwa visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Dress genuinely modestly — Siwa is a conservative, traditional community, more so than Cairo or the Red Sea resorts.
Carry genuinely cash — Siwa has very limited card acceptance and few ATMs.
Book genuinely a Great Sand Sea safari through a reputable local guide.
Pack genuinely for cold desert nights, even if the day has been hot.
Bring genuinely a good book or two — Siwa's real pleasure is its slow pace.
Respect genuinely local customs around photographing Siwan women without permission.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Siwa?
faq.a: Two to three days genuinely covers the main sights, though the journey itself makes a longer stay worthwhile.

faq.q: How do you get to Siwa?
faq.a: Genuinely by long-distance bus from Cairo, or a shorter road trip via Marsa Matrouh on the north coast.

faq.q: Is Siwa worth the long journey?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — its culture, ruins and landscape are unlike anywhere else in Egypt.

faq.q: What language is spoken in Siwa?
faq.a: Siwan, genuinely a Berber (Amazigh) language distinct from Egyptian Arabic, though Arabic is widely understood.

faq.q: Can you combine Siwa with the White Desert?
faq.a: It's genuinely possible but demanding — the two sit on opposite sides of the Western Desert, so most visitors choose one or budget significant extra travel time for both.
Yes, genuinely — Siwa is a well-established, welcoming destination, though it sits in a border region, so it's worth checking current travel advice before an independent trip.
